page: Amazon Web Services c6in.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors. Configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores running at 3.5 GHz, the instance delivers dedicated compute allocation supported by 54 MB of L3 cache. It includes 64 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support features AVX-512 with VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA extensions for vector processing and cryptographic operations.

Network performance is a core design focus, delivering a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring all persistent and non-volatile data storage to run over network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes. Benchmark testing positions the c6in.8xlarge consistently in the median tier across multi-threaded and single-threaded operations, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,044, a PassMark CPU score of 36,688.86, and 31.1 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 147.72 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read blocks and 66.69 GB/sec for uncached writes.

From a cost-efficiency and architecture standpoint, the instance balances high processor density with network capability. It is constrained by a lack of local NVMe storage and limited memory per core, making it less viable for memory-heavy databases or large parameter model inference, as indicated by lower throughput on 70B LLM workloads. The configuration is primarily matched for network-intensive batch processing, clustered scientific computing, distributed analytics nodes, high-traffic web serving fleets, and CI/CD compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.5 GHz 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processor built on the Nitro System. It provides 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 64 GB of DDR4 system memory, reflecting a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The platform incorporates a 50 Gbps baseline network interface, delivering substantial network throughput for distributed environments. The instance contains no bundled local NVMe storage, relying fully on EBS network storage. Benchmark evaluations reflect steady mid-range performance, with multi-core Geekbench scores of 14,044, PassMark CPU ratings of 36,688.86, and static web serving throughput reaching 34.98 GB/sec. Given its compute density and network bandwidth, the c6in.8xlarge is suited for network-heavy distributed applications, backend microservices, software compilation jobs, and high-concurrency web tiers.
